references.text: Job describes security and rest without fear, where no one will terrify—the same promise of peace and protection as in Leviticus 26:6.
Isaiah prophesies about the absence of wild animals in the restored land, parallel to the promise to remove dangerous beasts from the land.
Ezekiel repeats God's promise of a covenant of peace where wild animals are removed and the people can live securely—a direct parallel to Leviticus 26:6.
The promise that no one will terrify them and that they will be safe from wild animals reflects the wording in Leviticus 26:6.
Hosea describes a covenant where God removes weapons of war and lets the people lie down securely—the same themes of peace, absence of swords, and secure rest.
Micah prophesies about a time when each man will sit securely under his vine and fig tree without anyone to terrify him—fulfillment of the promise of peace without fear.
Zephaniah promises that the remnant of Israel will rest without anyone to terrify them—the same expression 'without anyone to terrify' as in Leviticus 26:6.
The psalmist expresses trust in lying down and sleeping in peace because the Lord gives security—a personal experience of the promise of peaceful rest.
Proverbs promises sweet sleep without fear for those who follow wisdom—the application of the promise of secure rest in wisdom literature.
Jesus gives his disciples his peace, a peace the world cannot give—spiritual fulfillment of the promise of shalom in the land.
